question: Should OpenClaw pursue distributed job orchestration as a core Gateway feature, a plugin-provided backend/API seam, or documentation for external orchestration while narrower cron/session/runtime issues proceed separately?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the right owner boundary, backend contract, config shape, failure semantics, observability surface, and dependency/security posture require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Orchestration
options.body: Define the shared scheduler/job ownership contract first, then decide whether Redis/BullMQ is one implementation behind that seam.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonical Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as prior art while cron HA, external session storage, and distributed runtime each own their narrower implementation decisions.

options.title: Document External-Orchestration Pattern
options.body: Decide not to add a core backend for now and document how production operators can run external queues or schedulers around OpenClaw safely.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Orchestration
recommendation.body: Define the shared scheduler/job ownership contract first, then decide whether Redis/BullMQ is one implementation behind that seam.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already gave keep-open architecture guidance on this issue and has recent history on the central cron scheduling path.
